# PLAN 1b.1 — joystick — Round 1 (Claude → Codex)

Plan rev 4.1 is at HEAD `5ce1dbc` (unchanged since your READY). The user decided on 2026-10-21:
(1) adopt the §9.1 annex as normative spec text; (2) approve `anchored-perspective-v1` for ordinary
Space; (3) confirm §19.2 Q2 neutral lighting, Q6 scene files only (Space share URLs deferred), Q5
desktop/laptop first (mouse, trackpad, keyboard; no Space touch; Plane keeps mobile) — and the user
ADDED: **"We should support joystick for exploration as well."**; (4) the §13.2 "(1b.2)" erratum.
Items 1, 2, 4 and the confirmations are mechanical (spec rev 4.2, plan rev 4.2). The joystick is new
scope and I want to co-design it with you before writing it into spec §13.3/§19.2 and the plan.

## My position

**Scope.** Browser Gamepad API, Space only in 1b.1: orbit (with dolly/pan) and flight, plus overview,
orientation reset and flight toggle on buttons. Plane deferred (§17): Plane's navigation is 1a-owned
(`bindPlaneNavigation`, T12) and §4.3 "Plane unchanged" makes any Plane input change non-cheap in 1b.1.
I will list Plane gamepad as a question for the user rather than settle it here.

**Ownership.** A new small task **B12b** (Codex, reviewer Claude), Node-only, after B12:
`src/space/gamepad.js` (pure: snapshot → intents) plus the minimal B12 hooks (a `gamepad` kind). B14
wires polling into the workspace frame callback and owns the browser check. Alternative: fold into B12
— I prefer the split so B12 stays as reviewed.

**Input contract.**
- Only `gamepad.mapping === 'standard'`; others are reported "unsupported mapping" and ignored. The
  first connected standard pad (lowest index) drives; others ignored.
- The API has no change events for axes and Chrome exposes a pad only after a button press on it. We
  poll `navigator.getGamepads()` (injected as `getGamepads`) **once per frame, in the same callback as
  `flight.tick(now)`**; no second rAF loop, no timers. A poll yields at most one preview
  (`gestures.grouped`/`flightUpdate`) per frame; render requests go through the scheduler's normal
  coalescing, so the render cadence and the 2-batch admission limit are untouched. No polling while
  the workspace is inactive or the document hidden.
- Mapping (standard layout): orbit mode — left stick yaw/pitch orbit about the focus; right stick Y
  dolly, right stick X pan-horizontal; D-pad up/down pan-vertical. Flight mode — left stick
  move/strafe, right stick look (yaw/pitch, upright, no roll), triggers (buttons 6/7, analog) descend/
  ascend along world Z, bumpers (4/5) halve/double speed (discrete, once per press). Buttons: Start (9)
  toggles flight (= `F`), B (1) stops flight (= Escape for flight), Back/Select (8) overview, Y (3)
  orientation reset. No focus on the pad in 1b.1 (needs a centre pick; defer).
- Dead zone: radial 0.15 on each stick, rescaled to [0, 1] outside it; triggers 0.05. Response curve:
  `sign · r²` after rescale (plan defaults, not spec constants). Rates: full deflection = the same
  angular/linear rates the keyboard nudge produces per second, times flight speed in flight.
- Connect/disconnect: `gamepadconnected`/`gamepaddisconnected` update a panel status; each poll also
  checks `connected`. Disconnect mid-motion has **blur semantics**: commit the last preview, zero
  velocity, release.

**History (§6).** Add `gamepad` to `SPACE_KINDS`. In orbit mode one continuous stick run is one
camera-history entry via the existing wheel-burst mechanism (`grouped('gamepad', camera)`,
`groupQuietMs = 200`): the run commits after all axes return inside the dead zone for 200 ms. In
flight mode the flight run is already the single entry; pad motion inside it adds none. Button jumps
(overview, reset) are camera-only jumps: one entry each, and first commit any open gamepad run. Arbiter
rule: one Space gesture at a time — while a pointer drag, key-repeat run or wheel burst is open, pad
motion is ignored, and vice versa (first owner wins; buttons that jump settle the open gesture first,
as Back/Forward does).

**Focus / activation.** Polling only after the activation token is current and prewarm verified;
`deactivate()` → `stopNavigation('deactivate')` commits an open gamepad run exactly once; blur and
`visibilitychange` likewise. Camera exterior status is computed on each **committed** camera as today
(not per polled frame).

**Accessibility.** Fixed documented mapping in 1b.1; remapping and invert-Y deferred (§17). Keyboard
and mouse remain complete alternatives.

**Testing without hardware.** Node: fake `Gamepad` snapshots (axes, `{pressed, value}` buttons,
`mapping`, `connected`, `timestamp`) and the fake clock drive `gamepad.js` and the B12 gestures.
Browser (B14, headed `shell` group): `page.addInitScript` replaces `navigator.getGamepads` with a
scripted fake and dispatches `gamepadconnected`. Never a real device in the gate.

**Exit criteria.** Named Node tests (e.g. `a stick run is one camera-history entry`, `inputs inside the
dead zone produce no motion`, `disconnect mid-run commits the last preview and zeroes velocity`,
`polling while inactive or hidden does nothing`, `a non-standard mapping is reported and ignored`,
`one poll produces at most one preview per frame`), and one headed check: `A scripted gamepad orbits
and flies, each run is one camera-history entry, and a disconnect stops flight`.

## Questions for you
1. Scope: agree Space-only (Plane deferred), or is Plane pan/zoom cheap enough to include?
2. B12b vs folding into B12; and is the browser wiring right in B14's `shell` group?
3. Mapping, dead zone, curve and the per-frame poll rule — any change?
4. History/arbiter semantics — any conflict with §6, B12's gesture rules or B14's activation contract?
5. Anything missing for the spec text (§13.3, §19.2 Q5)?

Please answer as a peer: agreed / changes, and say whether the result, as amended by your changes, is
**READY** as a plan amendment (rev 4.2). Read-only; no edits.

## Codex — PLAN 1b.1 — joystick — Round 1 reply (run 20261021T033701Z-268a, resume of 20261021T012346Z-8408)
*2026-10-20 20:43:49 PDT*

**NOT READY yet.** I agree with Space-only and B12b. The remaining scope issue is that **standard-gamepad support may exclude the joystick the user intends**. The engineering amendment is otherwise ready to draft with the changes below.

**1. Scope — agree Space-only; counter standard-only as an interpretation of “joystick.”**

Plane support adds activation, input ownership and history obligations. Keep it deferred in §17; I would not reopen that boundary without an explicit request.

The Gamepad API also represents joysticks, but `mapping === 'standard'` specifically means the controls follow the standard gamepad layout. A browser-exposed joystick can have `mapping === ''`. Rejecting that device is defensible for a documented standard-gamepad feature, but does not necessarily satisfy this user’s request. [W3C Gamepad specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/gamepad/#scope), [mapping definition](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Gamepad/mapping).

Carry **one user question**, replacing the proposed Plane question:

> Which controller model(s) do you intend to use? Is standard-gamepad support sufficient for 1b.1, or must a joystick/flight stick with a non-standard layout work?

If the latter, B12b needs an explicit mapping profile and B14 needs a way to configure/select it. We must not guess that device’s axes and buttons. Deferring all remapping then becomes incompatible with the required scope.

**2. Task ownership and integration — agree B12b and B14, with explicit interfaces.**

Keep **B12b: Codex, reviewer Claude**, after B12; make B14 explicitly depend on it. Pure snapshot decoding and the input state machine belong in B12b; browser polling, status and wiring belong in B14. The headed `shell` group is correct when the check exercises the real Space renderer.

Add this B12 flight hook:

```js
flight.setAnalogInput({forward, strafe, rise, yaw, pitch})
```

Its components are normalized demands. `flight.tick(now)` remains the sole continuous flight-camera writer; `stop()` clears the analog demands as well as keyboard state. The controller adapter must not also call `flightUpdate` independently in the same frame.

For orbit, compose all active orbit/pan/dolly demands into one pose and submit one preview. A jump action suppresses continuous motion for that frame. This makes the “at most one controller-driven camera update per frame” rule executable.

**3. Mapping, response and polling — mostly agree, with these changes.**

Your standard mapping is acceptable. Document control positions alongside Xbox-style labels, and freeze axis signs. Button actions use rising edges; held bumpers must not repeatedly multiply speed.

Make the radial curve precise. For stick vector `v`, `r = hypot(v.x, v.y)` and `d = 0.15`:

```text
r ≤ d: output = (0, 0)
otherwise: output = (v / r) · ((min(r, 1) − d) / (1 − d))²
```

This squares the magnitude while preserving direction. For triggers, use the analogous scalar curve with dead zone `0.05`. Missing or non-finite input values cannot perpetuate a previous motion demand.

B12 does not currently freeze “keyboard rates per second.” Replace that reference with explicit controller defaults:

- Orbit and flight look: **π/2 radians/s** at full deflection.
- Orbit pan: **½ the visible focus-plane height/s**.
- Dolly: exponential distance change, **doubling/halving per second**.
- Flight translation: the explicit flight speed; cap the combined translation vector’s magnitude at one. **Flight speed does not multiply angular speed.**

Speed buttons use the same validated range as the speed control.

Agree one poll per workspace animation frame, before the flight tick, without another loop or timer. However, this input callback must continue while controller input is enabled **even when rendering is idle**. Integrate elapsed seconds, retain B12’s 100 ms clamp, and reset the time baseline on suspension.

Do not use an unchanged `Gamepad.timestamp` to suppress held-stick movement: it describes input updates, not the passage of simulation time. [W3C timestamp definition](https://www.w3.org/TR/gamepad/#dom-gamepad-timestamp).

Replace the Chrome/button-only assertion with:

> Browser exposure may require controller interaction. Show “Press a controller button to connect”; the discovery interaction itself performs no navigation action.

The specification allows qualifying axis interaction too. [W3C controller exposure rules](https://www.w3.org/TR/gamepad/#dom-navigator-getgamepads).

**4. History, ownership and activation — agree on outcomes; refine the mechanism.**

The wheel-burst timer is insufficient for controller runs. A delayed frame must not split a continuously held stick into two history entries.

Use this replacement:

> An orbit controller run begins on the first accepted non-neutral motion and updates one `gamepad` gesture. It commits after motion controls have been observed neutral for 200 ms. The neutral interval starts from an observed neutral sample, not from the last camera preview. Suspension or disconnection commits immediately.

“Motion controls” includes D-pad and triggers where applicable. B12b can use `drag('gamepad', camera)` / `dragCommit('gamepad')`, or equivalent explicit begin/update/commit hooks; it should not inherit wheel inactivity semantics.

Additional lifecycle rules:

- **Input eligibility:** current activation token, successful prewarm, ready workspace, visible document, focused window, and viewport navigation enabled. Parameter editing and modal dialogs suspend controller navigation.
- **Neutral re-arming:** after connection, resume, controller replacement, mode change or ownership loss, require neutral motion controls and released action buttons before accepting new input. Held controls must not restart movement on reactivation.
- **Stable selection:** choose the lowest eligible index initially, then retain that controller until it disconnects. A newly connected controller must not steal control; a replacement starts disarmed.
- **Separate source ownership from history ownership:** the `flight` history gesture can remain open while control passes between desktop input and controller input. Do not mistake an existing flight gesture for an incompatible owner that rejects every controller sample.
- **Stopping overrides ownership:** Escape, stop, suspension and selected-controller disconnection always work. Overview/reset first stop navigation and commit the current run, then apply their single camera jump. They must not leave a flight tick able to move the new camera.
- Disconnection of an **unselected** controller changes status only.

Extend the documented stop reasons with `disconnect` and `input-suspended`; both clear demands and commit once. Camera exterior classification remains on committed cameras.

**5. Spec coverage and verification — extend the amendment slightly.**

Update §3’s release row and §6’s gesture rule as well as §13.3/§19.2; add controller disconnection to §15 and the agreed exclusions to §17. Controller selection, button state and mapping preferences are runtime/input settings, outside `atlas.scene`.

The normative navigation text should include:

> For supported controller layouts, Space provides controller-driven orbit, pan, dolly and basic flight. Continuous controller navigation follows the camera-history rules. Losing input eligibility or the selected controller stops movement and commits the last preview exactly once. Resuming requires neutral controls. Mouse and keyboard remain complete alternatives.

Handle a missing API and `getGamepads()` throwing `SecurityError` as controller-unavailable states without disabling other navigation. An empty list is not proof that no controller is attached. [MDN `getGamepads()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/getGamepads).

Keep your tests and add these consequential cases:

- Held deflection across a delayed frame remains one history entry.
- Equal-duration constant input at different frame rates produces equivalent movement.
- Held controls across blur, workspace switching or controller replacement cause no resumed movement.
- Flight receives one update per frame; overview/reset stops it before the jump.
- Ownership conflicts, button edges and unselected-controller disconnection behave as specified.
- API absence/denial preserves mouse and keyboard navigation.

The scripted headed check is appropriate gate evidence for integration. Describe physical-device compatibility as unqualified until an actual device has been exercised; hardware need not become a gate dependency.

**Agreed so far**

- Space-only scope; Plane controller navigation deferred.
- B12b owned by Codex, reviewed by Claude; B14 owns browser integration.
- Your standard-layout mapping, dead-zone defaults and squared response.
- One input frame callback, existing scheduler admission, camera-only history and complete desktop alternatives.
- Synthetic tests without mandatory controller hardware.

**Still disputed**

- Whether standard-only support satisfies the user’s joystick request. If confirmed, I am **READY with the engineering changes above**. If an unmapped joystick is required, mapping support must join B12b/B14 before the amendment is READY.

## A. Round-1 findings 1-7 (verbatim). For each, answer ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED with file:line evidence.

1. **Important — Replacement can resume rendering while the context is still lost.** [src/app.js:489](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:489)  
   An export timeout sets `retired`; after release, line 518 immediately replaces the renderer despite `adapter.unavailable`. GPU construction fails on the lost context, CPU fallback clones the canvas, and replacement clears unavailability. The same problem occurs with **loss → restoration while leased → another loss → release**, because `pendingReplacement` retains the earlier restoration.

   Track actual context restoration separately from the adapter’s availability latch. Replace only after the current loss has been restored and the lease released. The proposed `reserved || unavailable` guard alone is insufficient: `unavailable` remains true until replacement, so it would also block legitimate restoration. Add regression checks for both sequences.

2. **Important — `lastReport` does not always describe the displayed image.** [src/app.js:75](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:75), [src/app.js:551](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:551)  
   There are two distinct gaps:

   - Render A, start navigation to B, then change appearance. `adapter.recolor()` changes the retained A image before checking geometry compatibility; it returns no report when B’s geometry differs. The app retains A’s old appearance report. If B fails, that mismatch persists.
   - Export rendering overwrites/resizes the canvas and clears `adapter.published`, but the app retains its interactive report. Loss and replacement likewise leave the old report exposed after its image/resources cease to be valid.

   Make displayed-image provenance authoritative in the adapter and synchronize the exposed report with it. A non-null report must describe the actual retained or export image; clear it when that cannot be established. Recolor must either produce truthful provenance for the retained geometry or defer painting. Add tests covering pending navigation plus recolor and failure, export encoding, loss, and replacement.

3. **Important — Saving during an export can pair live settings with export pixels.** [src/app.js:415](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:415)  
   Hold export encoding, change only the palette, then save a discovery. The appearance edit is deferred by the lease, while `busy` and `dirty` can both remain false. The saved settings describe the new palette; the thumbnail contains the export’s old palette.

   Fix now: reject capture while reserved, unavailable, or retired, and require a valid publication matching the saved scene. T12 replacing this path is not a reason to leave the mismatch operational meanwhile.

4. **Important — Destroying loss-invalidated GL objects contaminates the restored context’s error state.** [src/app.js:495](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:495)  
   After restoration, `previous.destroy()` calls deletion methods with objects invalidated by the loss. These calls generate `INVALID_OPERATION`; this is more than console noise. T00b’s `drainWebGL` explicitly rejects a pending GL error before creating its fence. That follows the [Khronos invalidated-object rules](https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/specs/latest/1.0/).

   Add loss-aware disposal: stop the old worker and settle its pending work without submitting invalid old handles to the restored context. Preserve normal destruction for valid resources. Do not hide the problem by consuming errors in the drain. If the fix changes frozen `renderer.js`, explicitly record that narrow exception as **PLAN/SPEC CHANGE**.

5. **Minor — Swallowing stage-hook exceptions can hide failed assertions.** [src/plane/export.js:25](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/plane/export.js:25)  
   I reproduced a hook that records each stage and then throws an assertion at every stage. All stage names are present, the export completes, and no error is exposed. A stage-presence assertion therefore does not necessarily catch a broken observer.

   Keep observer exceptions isolated from the export outcome and lease release, but expose them through a diagnostic error collection or callback that tests assert is empty. **PLAN/SPEC CHANGE:** finalize Amendment F’s observer-error contract accordingly.

6. **Important — Amendments G(3) and H still need the application lifecycle contract.** [src/app.js:548](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:548), [tests/workflow.mjs:342](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/tests/workflow.mjs:342)  
   There is no asynchronous completion signal or directly queryable current device epoch/state. An old report’s epoch is not the current device epoch. The workflow finalizer also still uses its older readback and silently accepts missing WebGL.

   **PLAN/SPEC CHANGE:** land the completion contract described below in the T08 fix round, expose current backend/epoch/availability, and complete expected-backend bookkeeping using T00b’s shared drain. A page expected to remain GPU-backed must fail if its drain returns `no-webgl`.

7. **Important — The specified recovery actions are missing.** [src/app.js:350](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:350), [src/app.js:516](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:516)  
   An interrupted export retains its request internally, but only displays a reason. Clicking Download again captures the live scene, not necessarily the interrupted snapshot. Restoration also requests another render on every restored event without a recovery-attempt limit.

   §14 and charter §3.10 require offering a restart of the retained job and stopping automatic retries after repeated loss. **PLAN/SPEC CHANGE:** add those actions and their tests to T08’s recovery contract; T12 must preserve them. This is an omission in the plan as well as the implementation.


Also report any NEW breakage in `git diff eb28ccd..7fc8ea4` (excluding T00b content from eba9aeb).

I reviewed **`eba9aeb..7fc8ea4`**, excluding the T00b implementation introduced by the merge.

**A. Round-1 findings**

| Finding | Disposition | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Replacement while still lost | **ADDRESSED** | [app.js:502](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:502) gates replacement on `contextLost` independently of `adapter.unavailable`. Workflow line 190 checks refusal during export and acceptance afterward. This still depends on fixing publication validity in finding 1. |
| 4. Loss-aware disposal | **ADDRESSED** | [renderer.js:57](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/plane/renderer.js:57) records loss; line 164 skips invalid GL deletions after stopping the worker and settling pending work. |
| 5. Hidden observer errors | **ADDRESSED** | [export.js:30](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/plane/export.js:30) collects errors; the returned array and entries are frozen. Unit and workflow checks assert the diagnostics without changing export outcome. |
| 6. Completion and lifecycle contract | **NOT ADDRESSED — partial** | [app.js:619](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:619) exposes the required device snapshot, and workflow line 369 enforces expected backends. Completion has the boundary/deadline defects below; browser/navigation bookkeeping remains outstanding. |
| 7. Restart and bounded recovery | **NOT ADDRESSED — partial** | [app.js:573](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:573) correctly restarts the retained scene and dimensions under a new identity. Automatic-recovery stopping is incomplete: findings 2–3 below. |

**Remaining and new findings**

1. **Important — Destructive render failures retain obsolete publication metadata.** [render-adapter.js:129](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/plane/render-adapter.js:129), [renderer.js:78](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/plane/renderer.js:78)

   Render A at 320 pixels, then resize or export at a larger width. `GpuRenderer.resize()` changes the canvas dimensions and reallocates its field before checking framebuffer completeness. If allocation fails, the adapter returns `failed` but retains A’s publication.

   I reproduced this using the actual `GpuRenderer.render/resize` methods with a fake GL: the canvas became 640 pixels while its publication still reported 320. The export path has the same problem. A same-scene resize failure can subsequently pass the discovery scene-equality check.

   **Fix:** invalidate publication and its completion ticket when a failure may have changed the canvas or field. Preserve the old publication only when retained-image validity is established. Test destructive interactive and export failures, not only fake failures that leave the image untouched.

2. **Important — The recovery pause does not prevent queued rendering.** [app.js:167](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:167), [app.js:154](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:154)

   `flushRender()` does not check `renderingPaused`. If navigation queued dirty work during the first recovery, a second loss can set the pause while the old render’s finalizer schedules that work. The queued flush then renders despite the pause. I reproduced this with the actual function.

   Separately, every `requestRender()` clears the pause, including requests originating from an active tour or resize. Those are not explicit recovery authorization.

   **Fix:** guard submission with `renderingPaused`; preserve queued desired state while paused; distinguish explicit resume/user navigation from automatic requests. Add pending-dirty-work and active-tour tests.

   **PLAN/SPEC CHANGE:** replace Amendment I’s “any render request clears the pause” with an explicit-user-action rule.

3. **Important — Recovery is declared successful before GPU completion.** [app.js:181](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:181)

   `recoveryAttempts` resets when `adapter.render()` returns application-side completion. The recovery draw can still be executing on the GPU. If that draw causes another device loss, the counter is already zero, permitting another automatic attempt indefinitely.

   I confirmed that the counter resets while the publication fence remains unsignaled.

   **Fix:** reset the recovery episode only after valid completion evidence for that recovery epoch—GPU queue completion or CPU paint. Test loss after submission but before fence completion; the existing held-worker test covers only pre-submission recovery.

   **PLAN/SPEC CHANGE:** define successful recovery using the completion signal, while preserving `rendered` and `whenIdle` as application-side facts.

4. **Important — Completion checks the wrong epoch after replacement and misses the final asynchronous boundary.** [render-adapter.js:164](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/plane/render-adapter.js:164)

   Two reproduced cases:

   - Await A, lose/replace the device, publish B, then resume polling: the result is `superseded`, because report inequality is checked before the captured ticket’s loss/epoch.
   - A loss between `awaitFence` resolving and `completion()` continuing still produces success. `evidence()` reads the **current** epoch, so an epoch-0 request can receive epoch-1 completion evidence.

   **Fix:** validate the captured ticket’s renderer/context/epoch/loss identity before publication identity, repeat validation after `await awaitFence(...)`, and construct evidence from captured identities. Add tests for replacement followed by a new publication and invalidation at the final continuation.

5. **Important — `whenDrawn` does not enforce one deadline through success.** [app.js:651](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:651), [completion.js:38](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/plane/completion.js:38)

   `whenIdle()` can observe idleness on its next 30 ms poll after the supplied deadline. `Math.max(1, remaining)` then grants fresh time; CPU completion can immediately succeed despite the expired overall deadline. I reproduced a 10 ms request succeeding after submission consumed 30 ms.

   `awaitFence()` also accepts a successful poll without checking whether the poll crossed its deadline.

   **Fix:** validate a positive finite bound at the entry point, reject exhausted remaining time, and check deadline/validity after polling and before returning success. Add submission-budget exhaustion and successful-poll-overrun tests.

**B. Completion-signal ruling**

**Not fully met.** These parts are correctly implemented:

- Fences are created at interactive, recolor, and export publication—not when completion is requested.
- Polling yields before the first and subsequent polls.
- Null/missing fences, `WAIT_FAILED`, unexpected statuses, ordinary timeout, and observed context loss reject.
- Loss drops invalid fence handles without polling or deleting them against the restored context.
- Retention is limited to the current publication.
- Reports remain immutable; completion evidence is separate.
- CPU completion uses synchronous-paint evidence.

Captured-identity validation and the single-deadline guarantee need findings 4–5.

## 3. Findings

1. **Contract gap: no production method creates or fills a model or points buffer.** Severity major, **BLOCKING**. `src/space/render/backend.js:18` (`BACKEND_METHODS`), spec §9 method list, annex "Allocator" bullet. Scenario: B08's `menger_distance(p, depth)` reads "boxes from a storage buffer" and `points.wgsl` takes "points in"; B09's `classifyEffectiveCamera(request)` runs `evaluate_points` and is Node-tested on the fake. The only production route to a handle is `configureTargets`; `allocate`/`stage` exist on the fake as test controls only, and B06 implements the frozen list. B08 and B09 would have nothing to call, and adding a method after B06 reopens `assertBackend`. Fix (ruling 8): add `allocate` to `BACKEND_METHODS`/`assertBackend` with `allocate({name, bytes, usage: 'storage' | 'uniform', data?: Uint8Array}) → handle` — initial contents supplied at creation (`mappedAtCreation`, no queue work, so no admission lease), immutable afterwards, counted by the tracked allocator, released with `release(handle)`; the fake's `allocationDescription` accepts `data` and sets `resource.staged = data.slice()`; `stage()` stays a test control for simulating GPU-written results. One contract test: `a model buffer allocated with initial data reads back its bytes and is counted`. This is a PLAN CHANGE (spec §9 list, annex Allocator bullet, B00 interface, B06 Produces); say if you disagree.

2. **The plan-named loss test does not verify "invalidated before notified".** Severity major, **BLOCKING**. `tests/unit/fake-backend.test.js:47`; `tests/support/fake-backend.mjs:166–169`. The assertions `diagnostics().state === 'unavailable'` and `currentEpoch() !== epoch` run inside the `onLoss` listener, and `invalidate()` catches every listener exception and writes `listener-error` to `log` by design. Probe: a listener that throws leaves the test green and one `listener-error` entry. Mutants that keep the epoch on loss or notify before invalidating both survive, so the annex property your ruling 4 relies on is unverified. Fix: capture `state` and `currentEpoch()` into locals inside the listener and assert them after `backend.lose(...)`; also assert `backend.log` has no `listener-error` entry in this test.

3. **The P3 manifest test enforces incompleteness.** Severity minor, **BLOCKING** because it is cheap and otherwise forces a later edit of B00's test file by the task that completes the manifest (hot-file rule: test files are single-owner). `tests/unit/space-contract.test.js:219,221,224` assert `readyForAcceptance === false`, `unresolved.length > 0`, `scene === null`. Fix: assert invariants instead — `readyForAcceptance === (unresolved.length === 0)`; every `unresolved` entry has `field`, `reason` and an `owner` task id; every scene has `scene !== null` or appears in `unresolved`; the frozen fields (output, three scene ids with `lightingQuality: 'full'` and `targetSamples: 8`, trials 3/5, the six targets, the 4 ms threshold, the inspection commands) keep their values. (b) `fake-backend.test.js:151`: the failed ticket asserts `queueCompletedAt === null` but not `timing.elapsedMs === null` (ruling 4's rule). (c) `backend.js:221`: `onAdvance` returning pending without one original id must be rejected — untested. 5. **Dead guard.** Severity trivial. `fake-backend.mjs:139`: after `invalidate()` clears `pending`, no settle can reach `state !== 'ready'` with a pending item; the guard is unreachable. Keep as defence or drop; add a comment either way.

## 4. Ruling proposals for Codex

Each says what is frozen now, what stays provisional with an owner, and whether it is a plan change. Rulings 1, 2, 7 and 8 need your agreement before B01/B06/B07/B09 start; the rest are clarifications you can apply in r2.

**(1) Pipeline ABI.** Freeze your schema with two corrections. `bindings[i]` is `@group(0) @binding(i)`; `slot` is the WGSL variable name and the batch's `inputs`/`outputs` key; types `uniform-buffer` (read), `storage-buffer` (read | read-write), `texture` (read), `storage-texture` (read | write | read-write), `sampler` (read); a `read-write` slot appears in both `inputs` and `outputs` under the same name. `uniformLayout = {byteLength (multiple of 16), fields: [{name, type, offset}]}` with scalar 4/4, `vec2` 8/8, `vec3` 12/16, `vec4` 16/16, `mat4x4<f32>` 64/16; no arrays or `mat3x3` in 1b.1 (B10 uses three `vec3` for the basis); batches supply `uniforms` as `{name: number | number[]}` matching the fields exactly, packed by offset. `constants` are WGSL `override` constants by name (`FIELD`). `kind: 'compute'` has `entryPoint`; `kind: 'render'` has `vertexEntryPoint` and `fragmentEntryPoint` instead (your proposal; validated by kind). B06 prepares with `layout: 'auto'`, so no binding `format` field is needed; B06/B08/B10/B11 register their concrete `pipelineId`s and slots with preparation assertions. PLAN CHANGE: the render entry split (B00 interface text); the rest is within B00's "freezes the descriptor schema" mandate.

**(2) `onAdvance`.** Freeze `createJobPlan({request, operations, onAdvance})` with `onAdvance(operation, completion, pendingOperations) → replacement pending[] | undefined`; `advance(operation, completion)` requires `completion = {epoch, elapsedMs, timestampMs?, targetMs?}` (evidence form only); failed or interrupted work never advances (the scheduler settles the job). Rules: reserved and completed operations are immutable; every pending id survives a replacement (completion barriers); a replacement may not bypass a dependency; new operations may depend on reserved ones. The scheduler passes `targetMs = batchTargetMs` with each completion; B09's `onAdvance` resizes pending batches toward it; `createBatch` enforces the hard bounds, so B07's "never above the hard bounds" holds by construction. PLAN CHANGE: B00 (signature) and one sentence in B07 ("adapts the next batch's bounds" becomes "advances the plan with `{epoch, elapsedMs, targetMs}`; the plan's `onAdvance` adapts").

**(3) AO failure reduction.** Freeze: if any AO sample is a numerical failure, pack `{status: numericalFailure, reason: none, subreason: none}`; otherwise among unresolved samples pack the lexicographic minimum `(reason, subreason)`. Order-independent, which B11's bit-identical-across-completion-orders check needs; the per-pixel flags are what B09 counts (`lightingFailures: {shadow, ao, both}`), sample counts are not encoded. The shadow channel has one ray and no tie. Add the JS reference `reduceLightingFailures(failures) → Failure | null` to `status.js` as B11's WGSL test vector (additive, cheap, r2). Clarifying amendment to B00's `packLightingStatus` text, not a plan change.

**(4) Epoch and timings.** Freeze: `currentEpoch()` returns 0 if and only if the backend is unavailable or destroyed; successful acquisitions receive strictly increasing integers ≥ 1; `createAdmission` already rejects epoch 0, so "no lease is possible without a device" is self-consistent. Tickets: completed → `{outcome: 'completed', reason: null, queueCompletedAt, timing: {method: 'queue-completion', elapsedMs, timestampMs?}}`; interrupted → `reason` is the loss reason, `queueCompletedAt: null`, `timing: {method: 'queue-completion', elapsedMs: null}`; failed → `reason` the error message, same nulls. B09 maps nulls to `UNAVAILABLE` in reports. Clarification (annex wording), not a plan change; pin it with finding 4(b) and finding 2.

**(5) Target set.** Freeze `configureTargets({epoch, layoutId, internalSize, outputSize}) → {epoch, layoutId, internalSize, outputSize, handles, descriptions}` with `handles[name]` a handle, or `[previous, next]` for `accumulation` indexed by sample parity, and `descriptions[name]` = `{name, width, height, format, bytesPerTexel, bytes}` at actual internal dimensions. Export `TARGET_LAYOUT_ID = 'space-targets-v1'` from `backend.js`; B06 returns the identical shape. Clarification of the B00 interface text.

**(6) Lighting values.** Freeze: `{normalFieldSamples: 6, shadowRays: 1, shadowSteps: 64, aoSamples: 5}` are both the settled defaults and the 1b.1 ceilings — nothing in 1b.1 lets a user raise them (B14's lighting control is direct/full only), B09's `resolveQuality` uses them as the settled values and zero for `direct`, and `createBatch` enforces them; raising any value is a recorded plan amendment. Keep the export name `LIGHTING_BOUNDS_DEFAULT` (B09 and B11 cite it); add the sentence to the B00 text. Clarification.

**(7) P3.** The plan asks B00 to freeze complete scenes and trajectories that need B02's codec and B05's camera rules, and asks B04 (wave 1) to hash predictions that need those same poses. Ruling: B00 freezes the **manifest schema and every rule**; **B04 materializes and hashes**; B09 proves the materialization decodes; B15 consumes by hash.
- Frozen now (B00 r2, in the manifest): output 1280 × 720; three scene identities with their settings — bulb `power: "8"`, 128 iterations; quaternion `C: ["-0.2", "0.8", "0", "0"]`, `kappa: "0"` (the spec's default); menger `depth: 2` — all `lightingQuality: 'full'`, `targetSamples: 8`, 512 steps, `sampling.seed: 1` (the only randomness in the workload; the harness has none); orbit: 30 s, yaw at 0.5 rad/s about world Z through `focusLocal = [0,0,0]`, starting from the overview pose, upright, request times `t_k = 16·k ms`, k = 0…1874 (my proposal — ≥ 30 drafts/s cannot be measured at the burst's 60 ms spacing; say if you prefer another cadence); burst: 400 requests at 60 ms along the same orbit continuing from the orbit's end pose; stress: 40 edits at 250 ms for 10 s alternating `parameters.power` 8 ↔ 7 (bulb), `parameters.kappa` "0" ↔ "0.5" (quaternion), `parameters.depth` 2 ↔ 1 (menger); the settled request is the automatic settle after the final orbit pose, timed from its creation; coverage checkpoints are the reports of orbit requests k ∈ {0, 625, 1250, 1874} and the settled image, compared by `rayTermination` counts to B04's prediction; screenshot checkpoints: the settled image per scene; warm-up: the cold trial (fresh page load, preparation, the full workload) is trial 1 and is recorded, warm trials run in the same page without reload; trials, targets, timing and classification as already written.
- Provisional, **owner B04** (wave 1): the serialized scenes (§5.2 JSON, hand-authored to the schema, no `src/` import), the poses per request time in the §5.2 camera format (overview = 2.5 × enclosing radius along Project 0 A.6, computed in B04's own `camera.js`; B05's `overview()` must agree within its test tolerance), `performance-predictions.json` and both sha256s; B04 flips `readyForAcceptance: true` and empties `unresolved`.

- Owner B15: the harness realization; consumes both files by hash.
PLAN CHANGE: the P3 paragraph ("B00 freezes a workload manifest containing the complete scenes…" → schema and rules in B00, materialization in B04) and B04's deliverables. The alternative, if you object to hand-authored scene JSON in `tests/reference/`, is B12 as owner (it has B02, B05 and B09) with B04's prediction generator run there; I prefer B04 for independence and schedule.

**(8) `allocate` on the production interface** (finding 1). Freeze `allocate({name, bytes, usage: 'storage' | 'uniform', data?}) → handle` in `BACKEND_METHODS`; initial contents at creation, immutable afterwards, no queue work, counted, released by `release`. PLAN CHANGE (spec §9 list, annex, B00, B06).

**(9) `retain`/`retire`.** Provisional, fake-only test controls; owner B09 declares at its design whether the renderer needs retained-owner references across `configureTargets` (keeping the previous `display` presentable under the pending mark after a resize) — if so, a one-line amendment adds them to `BACKEND_METHODS` before B06 is reviewed; otherwise they stay backend-internal (B06's allocator).

## 3. Findings

1. **Contract gap: no production method creates or fills a model or points buffer.** Severity major, **BLOCKING**. `src/space/render/backend.js:18` (`BACKEND_METHODS`), spec §9 method list, annex "Allocator" bullet. Scenario: B08's `menger_distance(p, depth)` reads "boxes from a storage buffer" and `points.wgsl` takes "points in"; B09's `classifyEffectiveCamera(request)` runs `evaluate_points` and is Node-tested on the fake. The only production route to a handle is `configureTargets`; `allocate`/`stage` exist on the fake as test controls only, and B06 implements the frozen list. B08 and B09 would have nothing to call, and adding a method after B06 reopens `assertBackend`. Fix (ruling 8): add `allocate` to `BACKEND_METHODS`/`assertBackend` with `allocate({name, bytes, usage: 'storage' | 'uniform', data?: Uint8Array}) → handle` — initial contents supplied at creation (`mappedAtCreation`, no queue work, so no admission lease), immutable afterwards, counted by the tracked allocator, released with `release(handle)`; the fake's `allocationDescription` accepts `data` and sets `resource.staged = data.slice()`; `stage()` stays a test control for simulating GPU-written results. One contract test: `a model buffer allocated with initial data reads back its bytes and is counted`. This is a PLAN CHANGE (spec §9 list, annex Allocator bullet, B00 interface, B06 Produces); say if you disagree.

2. **The plan-named loss test does not verify "invalidated before notified".** Severity major, **BLOCKING**. `tests/unit/fake-backend.test.js:47`; `tests/support/fake-backend.mjs:166–169`. The assertions `diagnostics().state === 'unavailable'` and `currentEpoch() !== epoch` run inside the `onLoss` listener, and `invalidate()` catches every listener exception and writes `listener-error` to `log` by design. Probe: a listener that throws leaves the test green and one `listener-error` entry. Mutants that keep the epoch on loss or notify before invalidating both survive, so the annex property your ruling 4 relies on is unverified. Fix: capture `state` and `currentEpoch()` into locals inside the listener and assert them after `backend.lose(...)`; also assert `backend.log` has no `listener-error` entry in this test.

3. **The P3 manifest test enforces incompleteness.** Severity minor, **BLOCKING** because it is cheap and otherwise forces a later edit of B00's test file by the task that completes the manifest (hot-file rule: test files are single-owner). `tests/unit/space-contract.test.js:219,221,224` assert `readyForAcceptance === false`, `unresolved.length > 0`, `scene === null`. Fix: assert invariants instead — `readyForAcceptance === (unresolved.length === 0)`; every `unresolved` entry has `field`, `reason` and an `owner` task id; every scene has `scene !== null` or appears in `unresolved`; the frozen fields (output, three scene ids with `lightingQuality: 'full'` and `targetSamples: 8`, trials 3/5, the six targets, the 4 ms threshold, the inspection commands) keep their values. Restructure the manifest per ruling 7.

4. **Test gaps shown by surviving mutants.** Severity minor, not blocking (please add in r2 alongside the above). (a) `fake-backend.mjs:221`: `acquire()` while ready must throw `unavailable` — your report claims it, no test. (b) `fake-backend.test.js:151`: the failed ticket asserts `queueCompletedAt === null` but not `timing.elapsedMs === null` (ruling 4's rule). (c) `backend.js:221`: `onAdvance` returning pending without one original id must be rejected — untested. (d) `backend.js:213`: `advance(op, {epoch: 2, elapsedMs: 1})` with a mismatched epoch — untested. (e) `space-contract.test.js:49`: add `pixels: 7` (below the area) beside `9`; `9` is already caught by the max at `backend.js:89`, so the equality at `:90` is untested.

5. **Dead guard.** Severity trivial. `fake-backend.mjs:139`: after `invalidate()` clears `pending`, no settle can reach `state !== 'ready'` with a pending item; the guard is unreachable. Keep as defence or drop; add a comment either way.

6. **`'space-targets-v1'` exists only as a literal.** Severity minor. `fake-backend.mjs:234`. B06 and B09 would each hardcode it. Fix (ruling 5): export `TARGET_LAYOUT_ID = 'space-targets-v1'` from `backend.js`; the fake imports it.

7. **Render pipelines cannot be described.** Severity minor (B06 is the first consumer). `backend.js:123–124`: one `entryPoint` and compute-only `validateBindings` in the fake (`fake-backend.mjs:191`). Fix per ruling 1.

8. **Storage-buffer access set.** Severity minor. `backend.js:116`: `'storage-buffer': ['read', 'write', 'read-write']` — WGSL storage buffers are `read` or `read_write`; there is no write-only buffer. Drop `'write'` for buffers (storage textures keep all three).

9. **Undocumented fake semantics.** Severity trivial. `fake-backend.mjs:112`: `'next'` and `'oldest'` are the same selection; the staging pool (`:279–289`) prefers replacing an idle smaller buffer over growing to two — both fine, both deserve a one-line comment. `backend.js:255`: `assertBackend` throws `invalid-descriptor` for a missing method; acceptable (the plan has no better code), note it in the error message.

10. **Tooling note for the merger (no action for Codex).** `scripts/run-unit.mjs` cannot run `--expect-fail` on an unregistered file, so every 1b.1 task's "Step 2" command will fail the same way until registration; the guarded in-process run is the practical RED. Expected registered total after B00: 264.

11. **Two completion forms in `advance`.** Severity minor. `backend.js:212–215` accepts `{outcome: 'completed'}` without evidence and `{epoch, elapsedMs}`. B07 only ever calls the evidence form. Fix per ruling 2: require `{epoch, elapsedMs}` (so the epoch check can never be bypassed), drop the outcome form.

## 4. Ruling proposals for Codex

Each says what is frozen now, what stays provisional with an owner, and whether it is a plan change. Rulings 1, 2, 7 and 8 need your agreement before B01/B06/B07/B09 start; the rest are clarifications you can apply in r2.

**(1) Pipeline ABI.** Freeze your schema with two corrections. `bindings[i]` is `@group(0) @binding(i)`; `slot` is the WGSL variable name and the batch's `inputs`/`outputs` key; types `uniform-buffer` (read), `storage-buffer` (read | read-write), `texture` (read), `storage-texture` (read | write | read-write), `sampler` (read); a `read-write` slot appears in both `inputs` and `outputs` under the same name. `uniformLayout = {byteLength (multiple of 16), fields: [{name, type, offset}]}` with scalar 4/4, `vec2` 8/8, `vec3` 12/16, `vec4` 16/16, `mat4x4<f32>` 64/16; no arrays or `mat3x3` in 1b.1 (B10 uses three `vec3` for the basis); batches supply `uniforms` as `{name: number | number[]}` matching the fields exactly, packed by offset. `constants` are WGSL `override` constants by name (`FIELD`). `kind: 'compute'` has `entryPoint`; `kind: 'render'` has `vertexEntryPoint` and `fragmentEntryPoint` instead (your proposal; validated by kind). B06 prepares with `layout: 'auto'`, so no binding `format` field is needed; B06/B08/B10/B11 register their concrete `pipelineId`s and slots with preparation assertions. PLAN CHANGE: the render entry split (B00 interface text); the rest is within B00's "freezes the descriptor schema" mandate.

**(2) `onAdvance`.** Freeze `createJobPlan({request, operations, onAdvance})` with `onAdvance(operation, completion, pendingOperations) → replacement pending[] | undefined`; `advance(operation, completion)` requires `completion = {epoch, elapsedMs, timestampMs?, targetMs?}` (evidence form only); failed or interrupted work never advances (the scheduler settles the job). Rules: reserved and completed operations are immutable; every pending id survives a replacement (completion barriers); a replacement may not bypass a dependency; new operations may depend on reserved ones. The scheduler passes `targetMs = batchTargetMs` with each completion; B09's `onAdvance` resizes pending batches toward it; `createBatch` enforces the hard bounds, so B07's "never above the hard bounds" holds by construction. PLAN CHANGE: B00 (signature) and one sentence in B07 ("adapts the next batch's bounds" becomes "advances the plan with `{epoch, elapsedMs, targetMs}`; the plan's `onAdvance` adapts").

**(3) AO failure reduction.** Freeze: if any AO sample is a numerical failure, pack `{status: numericalFailure, reason: none, subreason: none}`; otherwise among unresolved samples pack the lexicographic minimum `(reason, subreason)`. Order-independent, which B11's bit-identical-across-completion-orders check needs; the per-pixel flags are what B09 counts (`lightingFailures: {shadow, ao, both}`), sample counts are not encoded. The shadow channel has one ray and no tie. Add the JS reference `reduceLightingFailures(failures) → Failure | null` to `status.js` as B11's WGSL test vector (additive, cheap, r2). Clarifying amendment to B00's `packLightingStatus` text, not a plan change.

**(4) Epoch and timings.** Freeze: `currentEpoch()` returns 0 if and only if the backend is unavailable or destroyed; successful acquisitions receive strictly increasing integers ≥ 1; `createAdmission` already rejects epoch 0, so "no lease is possible without a device" is self-consistent. Tickets: completed → `{outcome: 'completed', reason: null, queueCompletedAt, timing: {method: 'queue-completion', elapsedMs, timestampMs?}}`; interrupted → `reason` is the loss reason, `queueCompletedAt: null`, `timing: {method: 'queue-completion', elapsedMs: null}`; failed → `reason` the error message, same nulls. B09 maps nulls to `UNAVAILABLE` in reports. Clarification (annex wording), not a plan change; pin it with finding 4(b) and finding 2.

**(5) Target set.** Freeze `configureTargets({epoch, layoutId, internalSize, outputSize}) → {epoch, layoutId, internalSize, outputSize, handles, descriptions}` with `handles[name]` a handle, or `[previous, next]` for `accumulation` indexed by sample parity, and `descriptions[name]` = `{name, width, height, format, bytesPerTexel, bytes}` at actual internal dimensions. Export `TARGET_LAYOUT_ID = 'space-targets-v1'` from `backend.js`; B06 returns the identical shape. Clarification of the B00 interface text.

**(6) Lighting values.** Freeze: `{normalFieldSamples: 6, shadowRays: 1, shadowSteps: 64, aoSamples: 5}` are both the settled defaults and the 1b.1 ceilings — nothing in 1b.1 lets a user raise them (B14's lighting control is direct/full only), B09's `resolveQuality` uses them as the settled values and zero for `direct`, and `createBatch` enforces them; raising any value is a recorded plan amendment. Keep the export name `LIGHTING_BOUNDS_DEFAULT` (B09 and B11 cite it); add the sentence to the B00 text. Clarification.

**(7) P3.** The plan asks B00 to freeze complete scenes and trajectories that need B02's codec and B05's camera rules, and asks B04 (wave 1) to hash predictions that need those same poses. Ruling: B00 freezes the **manifest schema and every rule**; **B04 materializes and hashes**; B09 proves the materialization decodes; B15 consumes by hash.
- Frozen now (B00 r2, in the manifest): output 1280 × 720; three scene identities with their settings — bulb `power: "8"`, 128 iterations; quaternion `C: ["-0.2", "0.8", "0", "0"]`, `kappa: "0"` (the spec's default); menger `depth: 2` — all `lightingQuality: 'full'`, `targetSamples: 8`, 512 steps, `sampling.seed: 1` (the only randomness in the workload; the harness has none); orbit: 30 s, yaw at 0.5 rad/s about world Z through `focusLocal = [0,0,0]`, starting from the overview pose, upright, request times `t_k = 16·k ms`, k = 0…1874 (my proposal — ≥ 30 drafts/s cannot be measured at the burst's 60 ms spacing; say if you prefer another cadence); burst: 400 requests at 60 ms along the same orbit continuing from the orbit's end pose; stress: 40 edits at 250 ms for 10 s alternating `parameters.power` 8 ↔ 7 (bulb), `parameters.kappa` "0" ↔ "0.5" (quaternion), `parameters.depth` 2 ↔ 1 (menger); the settled request is the automatic settle after the final orbit pose, timed from its creation; coverage checkpoints are the reports of orbit requests k ∈ {0, 625, 1250, 1874} and the settled image, compared by `rayTermination` counts to B04's prediction; screenshot checkpoints: the settled image per scene (the cadence, the edit alternations and the checkpoint indices are my proposals, like the 16 ms spacing — the plan states none of them; counter-propose freely, but each must be frozen before B04 materializes); warm-up: the cold trial (fresh page load, preparation, the full workload) is trial 1 and is recorded, warm trials run in the same page without reload; trials, targets, timing and classification as already written.
- Provisional, **owner B04** (wave 1): the serialized scenes (§5.2 JSON, hand-authored to the schema, no `src/` import), the poses per request time in the §5.2 camera format (overview = 2.5 × enclosing radius along Project 0 A.6, computed in B04's own `camera.js`; B05's `overview()` must agree within its test tolerance), `performance-predictions.json` and both sha256s; B04 flips `readyForAcceptance: true` and empties `unresolved`.
- Owner B09: one Node test, `the P3 scenes decode through the Space codec and the poses are valid cameras` (B09 is the first task with the codec and request creation together).
- Owner B15: the harness realization; consumes both files by hash.
PLAN CHANGE: the P3 paragraph ("B00 freezes a workload manifest containing the complete scenes…" → schema and rules in B00, materialization in B04) and B04's deliverables. The alternative, if you object to hand-authored scene JSON in `tests/reference/`, is B12 as owner (it has B02, B05 and B09) with B04's prediction generator run there; I prefer B04 for independence and schedule.

**(8) `allocate` on the production interface** (finding 1). Freeze `allocate({name, bytes, usage: 'storage' | 'uniform', data?}) → handle` in `BACKEND_METHODS`; initial contents at creation, immutable afterwards, no queue work, counted, released by `release`. PLAN CHANGE (spec §9 list, annex, B00, B06).

**(9) `retain`/`retire`.** Provisional, fake-only test controls; owner B09 declares at its design whether the renderer needs retained-owner references across `configureTargets` (keeping the previous `display` presentable under the pending mark after a resize) — if so, a one-line amendment adds them to `BACKEND_METHODS` before B06 is reviewed; otherwise they stay backend-internal (B06's allocator).

## 1. Your round-2 findings 1–5 and the PLAN/SPEC CHANGE items, verbatim

For each numbered finding, answer ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED, with evidence (file:line, what you ran).

1. **Important — Destructive render failures retain obsolete publication metadata.** [render-adapter.js:129](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/plane/render-adapter.js:129), [renderer.js:78](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/plane/renderer.js:78)

   Render A at 320 pixels, then resize or export at a larger width. `GpuRenderer.resize()` changes the canvas dimensions and reallocates its field before checking framebuffer completeness. If allocation fails, the adapter returns `failed` but retains A’s publication.

   I reproduced this using the actual `GpuRenderer.render/resize` methods with a fake GL: the canvas became 640 pixels while its publication still reported 320. The export path has the same problem. A same-scene resize failure can subsequently pass the discovery scene-equality check.

   **Fix:** invalidate publication and its completion ticket when a failure may have changed the canvas or field. Preserve the old publication only when retained-image validity is established. Test destructive interactive and export failures, not only fake failures that leave the image untouched.

2. **Important — The recovery pause does not prevent queued rendering.** [app.js:167](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:167), [app.js:154](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:154)

   `flushRender()` does not check `renderingPaused`. If navigation queued dirty work during the first recovery, a second loss can set the pause while the old render’s finalizer schedules that work. The queued flush then renders despite the pause. I reproduced this with the actual function.

   Separately, every `requestRender()` clears the pause, including requests originating from an active tour or resize. Those are not explicit recovery authorization.

   **Fix:** guard submission with `renderingPaused`; preserve queued desired state while paused; distinguish explicit resume/user navigation from automatic requests. Add pending-dirty-work and active-tour tests.

   **PLAN/SPEC CHANGE:** replace Amendment I’s “any render request clears the pause” with an explicit-user-action rule.

3. **Important — Recovery is declared successful before GPU completion.** [app.js:181](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:181)

   `recoveryAttempts` resets when `adapter.render()` returns application-side completion. The recovery draw can still be executing on the GPU. If that draw causes another device loss, the counter is already zero, permitting another automatic attempt indefinitely.

   I confirmed that the counter resets while the publication fence remains unsignaled.

   **Fix:** reset the recovery episode only after valid completion evidence for that recovery epoch—GPU queue completion or CPU paint. Test loss after submission but before fence completion; the existing held-worker test covers only pre-submission recovery.

   **PLAN/SPEC CHANGE:** define successful recovery using the completion signal, while preserving `rendered` and `whenIdle` as application-side facts.

4. **Important — Completion checks the wrong epoch after replacement and misses the final asynchronous boundary.** [render-adapter.js:164](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/plane/render-adapter.js:164)

   Two reproduced cases:

   - Await A, lose/replace the device, publish B, then resume polling: the result is `superseded`, because report inequality is checked before the captured ticket’s loss/epoch.
   - A loss between `awaitFence` resolving and `completion()` continuing still produces success. `evidence()` reads the **current** epoch, so an epoch-0 request can receive epoch-1 completion evidence.

   **Fix:** validate the captured ticket’s renderer/context/epoch/loss identity before publication identity, repeat validation after `await awaitFence(...)`, and construct evidence from captured identities. Add tests for replacement followed by a new publication and invalidation at the final continuation.

5. **Important — `whenDrawn` does not enforce one deadline through success.** [app.js:651](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/app.js:651), [completion.js:38](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T08-r1/src/plane/completion.js:38)

   `whenIdle()` can observe idleness on its next 30 ms poll after the supplied deadline. `Math.max(1, remaining)` then grants fresh time; CPU completion can immediately succeed despite the expired overall deadline. I reproduced a 10 ms request succeeding after submission consumed 30 ms.

   `awaitFence()` also accepts a successful poll without checking whether the poll crossed its deadline.

   **Fix:** validate a positive finite bound at the entry point, reject exhausted remaining time, and check deadline/validity after polling and before returning success. Add submission-budget exhaustion and successful-poll-overrun tests.

**2. Proposed allocation annex text**

In spec §9’s method list, replace:

```text
prepare(pipelineSet)           → asynchronous, with progress events
configureTargets(targetDesc)   → allocates through the tracked allocator
```

with:

```text
prepare(pipelineSet)           → asynchronous, with progress events
allocate({name, bytes, usage, data?}) → opaque buffer handle
configureTargets(targetDesc)   → allocates through the tracked allocator
```

Replace the **Allocator** bullet in both spec §9.1 and the plan’s annex with:

> **Allocator.** Every application-owned allocation passes through the tracked allocator, which checks `tracked + bytes ≤ 1 GiB` before resource creation. The production method `allocate({name, bytes, usage, data?}) → handle` creates a buffer in the current available device epoch. `name` is nonempty; `bytes` is a positive safe integer divisible by four; `usage` is `'storage'` or `'uniform'`; optional `data` is a `Uint8Array` whose byte length does not exceed `bytes`. Initial data is defensively copied at creation and remaining bytes are zero. WebGPU initializes supplied contents through `mappedAtCreation`, copies them into the mapped range, and unmaps before returning; this performs no application queue submission and consumes no admission lease. The backend derives native usage flags, including copy-source support for readback. There is no production host-update method; admitted shader writes to storage buffers remain permitted. `stage()` is a fake-only test control.
>
> `release(handle)` marks a resource retiring; bytes leave accounting only when every ticket, mapping and retained-owner reference has ended. Uniform uploads, query/resolve storage, staging and model buffers are counted. `diagnostics()` reports `{state, epoch, tracked, peak, retiring, inventory}` using actual allocation sizes. Plane allocations remain separate.

Also add `maxUniformBufferBindingSize` to the annex’s recorded/checked limits, alongside `maxStorageBufferBindingSize`.

**A. Recovery hold seam: ACCEPT.**

It explicitly delays the application’s confirmation observer without fabricating completion evidence or bypassing epoch validation. The workflow releases and clears it. Holding confirmation establishes an *unconfirmed recovery* deterministically; it makes no claim that the GPU remains busy.

The shared `recovered(evidence)` path also fixes the observer-order race: my check confirmed that `whenDrawn` closes recovery even while the application’s independent observer remains held.

**B. Late evidence closing recovery: ACCEPT.**

A caller’s timeout and confirmed device completion are separate facts. Valid evidence from the current epoch can close recovery even when its delivery misses the caller’s deadline. An adapter rejection supplies no such evidence, and old-epoch evidence must not reset recovery. The implementation preserves both distinctions; my late-delivery and old-epoch checks passed.

**Amendment I:** The revised text matches the scoped implementation, including the final deadline checks, either observer closing recovery, narrowed resume actions and recovery test seam. No further plan/spec change is needed.

**New findings:** None introduced by `c6706b3..c899416`.

The gate record matches the reported failure. The saved probe output records twelve second-before-first observations; it supports the observer-order explanation without proving the proposed timer-clamping mechanism.

## Codex → Claude — EXEC T10 review r1 — IndexedDB persistence — VERDICT: CHANGES REQUIRED
*2026-10-21 00:11:18 PDT*

VERDICT: CHANGES REQUIRED

Spec compliance: ❌ overall. The §14 write guarantees are implemented correctly: one transaction per batch, success only on `complete`, rollback on abort, no fallback store, and no cancellation-induced false success. However, pagination can hide a stored discovery, and rejected opens can subsequently perform upgrades. Both problems are inherited from our plan code; I regard them as corrections we own together.

1. **Important — PLAN/SPEC CHANGE — pagination can make a surviving discovery unreachable.**  
   [src/shared/persistence.js:81](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T10-r1/src/shared/persistence.js:81)

   With 51 discoveries, controller A loads the first 50. Another source/connection deletes a discovery from that page. A then requests cursor `"50"`: the remaining dataset has 50 records, so it receives nothing and `nextCursor: null`. The last discovery remains stored but inaccessible through “Show more.”

   I reproduced this through T09’s actual controller/local-source code and its fake persistence. Notifications belong to each source instance; the other source’s deletion does **not** refresh A. Therefore, the report’s automatic-refresh justification is insufficient.

   **Fix now in T10:** use an opaque cursor anchored to the last ordering key, including an ID tie-breaker, rather than an offset. Align the fake and add concurrent insertion/deletion and equal-timestamp tests. T09’s public cursor interface can remain unchanged; amend the plan’s implementation blocks. T12 should retain a browser integration regression.

2. **Important — PLAN/SPEC CHANGE — an already rejected open still performs its upgrade.**  
   [src/shared/persistence.js:24](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T10-r1/src/shared/persistence.js:24)

   Hold a version-1 connection, request version 2, receive `blocked`, then release the original connection. The pending request proceeds through `onupgradeneeded`; closing its eventual successful connection does not undo the version change. Subsequent version-1 opens fail. This follows IndexedDB’s [open and upgrade algorithms](https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#open-a-database-connection). My scripted reproductions confirmed that both blocked and timed-out opens still execute schema creation without attempting an abort.

   **Fix now in T10:** when `onupgradeneeded` arrives after settlement, abort its upgrade transaction before making schema changes. On timeout, also attempt to abort an outstanding upgrade transaction. Retain late-success closure; an upgrade already committed before timeout cannot be undone.

   Extend the real blocked-upgrade check to verify the version after unblocking. Its cleanup currently accepts `deleteDatabase.onerror` and `onblocked` as success at [tests/workflow.mjs:134](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T10-r1/tests/workflow.mjs:134); require successful deletion so a leaked connection cannot escape detection.

3. **Minor — accepted numeric cursors can throw inside the callback and leave reads pending.**  
   [src/shared/persistence.js:63](/mnt/ml_storage/dev/projects/mandelbrot_explorer-wt/review-1a-T10-r1/src/shared/persistence.js:63)

   Cursor `"4294967296"` passes validation but exceeds `advance()`’s enforced unsigned-long range. The exception occurs in `onsuccess`, outside the promise executor; the read neither resolves nor rejects through this code. I reproduced that pending result with a scripted cursor. The API range is specified by [IDBCursor](https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#interface-idbcursor).

   **Fix alongside #1:** validate the replacement cursor completely and reject cursor-handler exceptions or transaction aborts. If offsets remain temporarily, reject values outside the supported range before starting the transaction.

The workflow edits are otherwise sound. Removing the two T10 insertions produces a file **byte-identical to the base**. Removing the new required pass produces the original suites manifest. Thus T05/T08 assertions, recovery hooks, CPU backend declaration, `drainExpecting`, and cleanup behavior are preserved. The new check is bounded, uses real IndexedDB from the application page, and asserts results before recording its pass. It is not vacuous. Its rollback assertions cover the old note and absent marker; strengthening them to compare the full old record, Blob contents, and stored report would improve the evidence.

For items **3 and 6**, my disposition is:

| Item | Decision |
|---|---|
| Deletion/pruning API | **Sufficient for T09b.** No `listWriteMarkers` is needed now. |
| 6(a): offset pagination | **Fix now, T10**, with T09 fake alignment and T12 integration coverage. |
| 6(b): late upgrade | **Fix now, T10**, as described in #2. |
| 6(c): silent `versionchange` closure | **Carry to T12.** Surface storage unavailability and an explicit recovery/reload path. Closing promptly is correct; subsequent operations currently fail truthfully. |
| 6(d): separate count/list transactions | **Carry to T12** as a consistency limitation. Do not treat `total` as proof that loaded pages are complete. If a matching snapshot is required, return page and count from one transaction and update T09’s adapter accordingly. |

T09b already holds the write IDs and must track definite-outcome delivery and outstanding reconciliation readers. It should retain every pending/checking/unknown entry, retain the newest 100 delivered definite outcomes, and delete eligible markers only after readers finish. Listing markers would not establish delivery or reader completion for another session, so it would not authorize sweeping orphaned markers.

One compatibility detail: T09b should call `commit({ puts: [], deletes })`; the current fake requires both arrays, whereas the real adapter supplies defaults. The controller also needs a local-source cleanup operation because it does not directly own the store. Those belong in T09b.

The Amendment D fit is otherwise good: definite result shapes match; marker absence returns `null`; cancelled marker reads reject with `AbortError`; controller destruction can stop observation without the adapter automatically aborting admitted writes.

All five hardening deviations are acceptable in intent:

- **Promise rejection for reads that cannot start:** accepted.
- **Not starting already-cancelled reads:** accepted.
- **Cursor/limit validation:** accepted, but incomplete as finding #3 shows.
- **Waiting for transaction abort after synchronous batch failure:** accepted and preferable. The already-finished abort fallback introduces no demonstrated false-success path.
- **Taking key paths from `STORES`:** accepted.

What I ran:

- Direct persistence tests: **3/3 passed**; `node --test` invocation also exited 0.
- Direct discoveries tests: **39/39 passed**.
- Syntax checks for persistence, its tests, and workflow; `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- Scripted transaction/read checks: complete-only success, pre/in-flight cancellation, post-commit cancellation, delayed failure settlement, cancelled marker reads, and closed connections: **passed**.
- Targeted reproductions: confirmed the pagination omission, late-upgrade execution, and oversized-cursor pending read.
- Independently inspected all three saved browser reports: **21 named passes each, no FAIL**.

I did not launch a browser or rerun the controller’s gate. The worktree remains unchanged; unit-manifest registration remains the merger’s job.

Agreed so far:

- Atomic writes, result semantics, deletion support, and preservation of prior workflow behavior are sound.
- Marker pruning belongs in T09b; no marker-listing API is required.
